summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with lower abdominal pain and found to have peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis, supported by elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cell count of 305 with 15% polymorphonuclear cells. She had recently stopped antibiotic prophylaxis due to a suspected allergic reaction. Initial treatment with IV vancomycin and cefepime was transitioned to intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime after clinical improvement and irrigation of the peritoneal cavity. Cultures and gram stains remained negative, but clinical and laboratory markers improved over the course of admission. She was discharged home to complete a 14-day course of intraperitoneal antibiotics with instructions for dwell technique and follow-up. Chronic conditions including type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and end-stage renal disease were managed with home medications throughout.
